task.title: Implement transcript-backed reasoning-path efficiency learning for AutoAgent
task.goal: Implement the smallest Phase 5F runtime slice that keeps AutoAgent manual and report_only while enabling explicit chat, transcript, and handoff evidence ingestion plus deterministic reasoning-path efficiency scoring in learning artifacts.

source.reference: user request in VS Code chat on 2026-04-12 to define the next concrete slice for real chat and handoff evidence plus straightest reasoning-path learning

constraints: Keep execution manual and report_only; do not enable autonomous continuation, autonomous apply-best, schedulers, queues, watchers, approval APIs, or execution-capable orchestration.
Keep guarded learning promotion review-only; do not auto-import, auto-apply, or auto-activate benchmark, mutation, or policy drafts.

Limit runtime changes to explicit chat, transcript, and handoff evidence ingestion plus deterministic reasoning-path efficiency scoring and reviewer-facing visibility; do not widen execution authority, auto-apply behavior, or approval authority.
Preserve existing evidence redaction, truncation, external-path controls, and explicit opt-in evidence-policy behavior from Phase 5A.
Do not introduce network calls, semantic LLM judging, opaque classifiers, or non-replayable heuristics.
Do not let the new reasoning-path signal directly bypass benchmark quality, terminal outcome, reviewed-policy runtime boundaries, apply-best authority, or continuation eligibility guardrails.
Keep governed artifacts under docs/agents/ and mirror touched files into the active run snapshot.
Do not commit secrets or write outside the governed docs/agents artifact flow.

decisions.summary: Selected a phased AutoAgent implementation path that starts with the target-bundle schema and loop-engine abstraction.

details.notes: The user chose the broad future optimization surface, but the implementation will start with the smallest governed slices that unblock later phases.

decisions.summary: Started Phase 1 by extending the AutoAgent loop from a single-target contract to a backward-compatible target-bundle model.

details.notes: The new contract supports optimizationTargets, target-aware mutations and checks, and bundle-aware apply-best behavior while keeping legacy experiments working.

details.notes: Focused tests now assert fail-fast behavior for missing target paths, duplicate target ids, and unknown targetId references in mutations and benchmark checks.

decisions.summary: Added governed evidence ingestion with privacy filtering and parse-error tolerance.

details.notes: The loop now emits a canonical autoagent-evidence dataset from current artifacts, run snapshots, and hook-audit JSONL while redacting secret-like values, normalizing repo-local paths, and recording malformed JSONL lines as parse errors instead of aborting the run.

decisions.summary: Expanded the Phase 1 experiment and report contract with staged-patch, provenance, richer policy blocks, and optional external debug-log ingestion.

details.notes: The loop now normalizes richer live-evaluator and continuous policy fields, reports staged-patch and provenance metadata, and can ingest explicitly configured VS Code or Copilot debug logs with the same redaction guarantees as governed evidence sources.

risk_register.risk: Live evaluator execution could introduce network-dependent flakiness or CI coupling.
risk_register.mitigation: Use an injectable evaluator adapter and fake implementation in tests; keep real provider calls out of deterministic test paths.

risk_register.risk: Evaluator output could override deterministic scoring in unsafe or opaque ways.
risk_register.mitigation: Limit execution to advisory and bounded tie-breaker semantics with deterministic scoring remaining primary.

risk_register.risk: Raw evaluator outputs could leak sensitive or noisy content into governed artifacts.
risk_register.mitigation: Keep raw output off by default and sanitize or truncate any retained content before serialization.

risk_register.risk: Frontier search could multiply candidate evaluations and generated artifacts faster than maintainers expect.
risk_register.mitigation: Keep frontier search bounded by candidatePolicy.frontierSize and leave current_best as the canonical default.

risk_register.risk: The replay ledger could drift from the report payload if later slices update search metadata in only one place.
risk_register.mitigation: Build the ledger from the same candidate records and frontier snapshots used by the main result object and keep focused assertions on both paths.

risk_register.risk: Resume checkpoints could drift from in-memory search state or accept stale experiment inputs, producing incorrect resumed results.
risk_register.mitigation: Build checkpoints from the live candidate records and frontier snapshots, and validate experiment, benchmark, mutation-catalog, and candidate-policy fingerprints before restoring state.

risk_register.risk: Compact checkpoints could reference generated candidate snapshots that are later deleted or moved, causing resume failures or partial restore.
risk_register.mitigation: Fail fast when a snapshot-backed candidate artifact is missing and keep the checkpoint contract scoped to the generated run root that owns those candidate snapshots.

risk_register.risk: The checkpoint manifest could drift from the actual resume restore contract or omit bundle target files if snapshot-path rules diverge.
risk_register.mitigation: Build the manifest from the same live checkpoint and candidate state used by resume and reuse the existing candidate snapshot-path helper for bundle expansion.

risk_register.risk: Checkpoint generation could accidentally capture post-live-evaluator winner state again, causing resume artifacts to drift from deterministic mutation-search semantics.
risk_register.mitigation: Freeze the deterministic best candidate before live evaluation runs and keep focused tie-breaker regression coverage that inspects emitted checkpoint and manifest artifacts directly.

risk_register.risk: Derived continuation readiness could drift from the governed review artifacts or silently treat unreadable review state as ready.
risk_register.mitigation: Use the machine-parseable governed state as the primary readiness source, classify unreadable or non-PASS review state with explicit blocked reasons, and keep focused regression coverage on missing or non-PASS review inputs.

risk_register.risk: docs/agents/state.json and docs/agents/review-report.md could diverge, causing continuation readiness to look approved even though the governed artifacts disagree.
risk_register.mitigation: Cross-check the machine-readable state and ReviewReport JSON block, surface explicit mismatch reasons, and keep readiness blocked unless the governed artifacts agree on PASS.

risk_register.risk: Maintainers could misread the top-level AutoAgentReport status as the current governed slice lifecycle even after docs/agents/state.json has already moved to Done and PASS.
risk_register.mitigation: Expose a separate governed lifecycle signal sourced from docs/agents/state.json and explain the distinction between artifact readiness and task lifecycle in canonical AutoAgent output.

risk_register.risk: Phase 3 could remain open-ended if the repository keeps adding visibility slices without a clear reviewed-handoff contract and explicit exit criteria.
risk_register.mitigation: Define a single stage-only reviewed continuation handoff contract and document explicit Phase 3 exit criteria that preserve manual/report_only behavior.

risk_register.risk: Post-Phase-3 orchestration work could blur planning and implementation boundaries, causing the repo to enable execution behavior before prerequisites and rollback constraints are explicit.
risk_register.mitigation: Use a planning-only slice to define prerequisites, rollout boundaries, and hard non-goals before any orchestration implementation is considered.

risk_register.risk: A staged orchestration contract could be misread as execution authority if the new metadata does not explicitly preserve manual and report_only semantics.
risk_register.mitigation: Keep the new orchestration layer additive, stage-only, and derived from reviewed handoff signals while exposing explicit blocked reasons, manual-only semantics, and out-of-scope execution wording in canonical artifacts.

risk_register.risk: Reviewed dispatch intent or approval posture metadata could be mistaken for an executable approval or dispatch workflow if the new slice does not keep approval state descriptive only.
risk_register.mitigation: Keep reviewedDispatchIntent and governedApprovalMetadata additive, manual, and report_only; expose approval metadata as governed-artifacts-only descriptive state; and keep explicit out-of-scope execution wording in canonical output.
